reason: Owns where the staged builder source lives and how ownership is proven: typed StagePlan/StageManifest/StageState, explicit caps, excluded prefixes and a binding check. It never copies or publishes, and tests cover the stage child, inventory and refusal paths.

Doc claims one backend precedence, but compose.rs and lib.rs also decide it (env override, declared backend, user preference), so 'which backend' has three entrypoints. from_engine coerces any non-Compose engine string to colima_nerdctl and a detection error falls back to colima_nerdctl, so a real unknown engine is re-labelled instead of staying unknown. The v0.14 legacy file is a bounded one-release read.

One resolver construction for the four catalog layers plus a typed CatalogServiceSource (service, catalog, source handle, layer, path). Retired user-global state is warned about once and never read or changed; errors propagate from the catalog and manifest layers.

One file holds Colima command specs, managed-profile resources and config parsing, user-facing notices, and compose argv builders. Compose argv is also built in compose.rs and session.rs, and profile listing is duplicated with exec/colima_runtime.rs:1034 and container_command/profile.rs:759. Four jobs in 713 lines with no module doc split; the observation classifier itself is typed (ColimaObservation).

Compose backend override and typed OsString argv builders are sound, but backend choice is decided again in backend.rs, and compose/exec argv is also built in colima.rs and session.rs. Consolidating the backend choice under backend.rs leaves this module as argv building only.

Namespace and state-root facade for the environment reconciler. state_home/state_root are typed Results and observe_root never creates state (R2), with the checkout-location rule stated once. Exercised by environment/tests.rs (23) and the activation tests.

The real backend seam (inventory, image ids, config hashes, containers-by-id) with typed Observed returns. Two problems: manager.rs keeps a second ContainerBackend trait with its own BackendId and capabilities for the same engines, and BackendError has only NotStarted/Uncertain, both carrying opaque strings, so a ten-method mutation seam cannot say whether it refused, timed out or failed. P: the trait pairs inventory/inventory_until, image_id/image_id_until and service_config_hashes_until with default ToolUnavailable arms, an inconsistent surface.

Owns the gate-scoped creation receipt: typed CreationRefusal variants, schema v5, image capability, and an explicit statement that the ID difference is inference, never an engine create response. Attached versus created ID expectations are separate fields, not a flag.

Names what the selected backend can actually observe about an image (resolved id, config hash, reference only) and refuses to promote a tag lookup into image identity. same_reference and digest_reference_binds make the comparison explicit.

The gate-scoped creation window: preflight observation, attached primary image re-observation, inventory difference and open/close around one apply. States the forged-label threat-model limit rather than implying authentication.

Fixes the expected inventory before apply and verifies it after: attached services must keep their IDs, expected creations must be new and exactly one workspace predecessor may stay or go, each refusal typed as Partial or ImageMismatch.
Corroborates nerdctl Compose network membership from frozen YAML and the container's own labels, refusing empty or unresolved names and unmatched alias sets rather than guessing membership.

The attachment surface: Hold ticket, typed HoldError (NotActive vs Env vs Run) and Idle reaping driven by settled holders rather than a timer. Persistent environments are borrowed, held ones reap on the last settlement.

Operations are typed and all serialise on the one EnvRun gate. But the same operation grows variants: reconcile, reconcile_observing, reconcile_in, reconcile_in_owned, activate, activate_with, each passing closures through another layer. Collapse the observing/owned variants into one parameterised entry point.

One owner for the environment run and gate, with an excellent typed EnvError (Busy, HeldBy, HostAuthorityRequired, Unsettled, Cleanup preserving the original cause). It is also the hottest module in the crate: 2,365 product lines and 78 commits in 30 days, carrying admission, parking, reacquire, settlement and integration-snapshot machinery, and it duplicates the parked/abort custody vocabulary that workspace_activation.rs also defines (ParkedEnvRun, EnvAdmissionOwner vs ParkedWorkspaceActivation, ParkedAbortCustody). Split admission/parking from the transition bodies.

The one environment record: pure read that returns Absent only with proof and Unknown otherwise, an unknown schema stays Unknown rather than being ignored, and protected() treats an unreadable holder list as protecting. Retention and state are typed enums.

Production remote custody for Colima and Docker: identity as engine:full-id@context, values never in argv, and four fixed shell helpers. Typed where it matters, but RemoteContainer::parse returns Option, so an unreadable identity and an absent one are the same fact (None); return the refusal reason instead. The four embedded shell payloads (HELPER, DOCKER_RELAY, COLIMA_RELAY, COLIMA_VM) are the bulk of the 1,167 lines.

A small typed run-bound executable/working-directory identity for sentinel recovery that explicitly holds no guest environment, credential or nonce, and verifies a record under a deadline. Only two tests exercise it (mean 6.5).

The status/doctor view for one environment: backend with its reason, record summary that names an unreadable record and treats unreadable holders as protecting, and a nothing_to_stop decision that requires proof of emptiness before skipping a stop.

Reserved workspace activation with custody before Env admission is the right design and its refusal types are explicit. Proportion is the problem: four begin variants (begin, begin_recoverable, begin_observing, begin_observing_recoverable) each repeat the same supervisor-id guard verbatim, apply has with/sealed/sealed-with-owner variants, one entry point carries #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)], and two unreachable! arms encode variant exclusivity. Parameterise the two axes instead of multiplying entry points.
Namespace for the exec layer: an explicit re-export surface, test-only clock capture behind the test-support feature, and no logic of its own. Churn is export-list updates as adapters were named.

Exact PID-file authority for profile recovery: O_NOFOLLOW open, dev/inode/mtime stability across the read, bounded text, PID range refusal, then SIGKILL only after re-reading the pidfile and re-checking process identity and limactl hostagent argv. Typed Observed verdicts; seven tests (mean 6.6) cover terminate and refusal paths.

Ensuring, observing, recovering and resetting the runtime, with typed RuntimeObservation and a progress phase enum. It re-owns managed Colima profile management that colima.rs:186 and container_command/profile.rs:759 also own (list_colima_profiles is defined in two files), and it carries paired entry points (ensure/_report, recover/_with_progress, reset/_with_progress) plus four capture variants. 1,268 product lines; proof is 24 tests at mean 6.7, mostly fixture oracles.
Turns the runtime's own progress lines into typed ComposeStepEvent, with the parse and service-name recovery in one place and table tests for the shapes both Docker Compose and nerdctl print.
Typed step bookkeeping (ComposeSteps, TimedStep, runtime_wait) so a finished step is never rewritten by a repeated line; small and covered by eight behaviour tests.
One owner for pruning stale health-check pidfiles, with an exported pattern, a stale minute bound and a typed prune result so the caller reports what it removed.

Named 'implementation' and holding four jobs: runtime/Compose capture, project and shared-container inventory, ownership verification, and workspace-artifact-builder observation and preparation. The same inventory job has nine entry points (list_running_compose_containers_for_policy{,_with_deadline,_with_timeout}, _for_project_with_deadline, _for_profile, _profiled, list_compose_containers_for_policy_including_stopped{,_with_deadline,_with_timeout}). 3,551 product lines with 80 commits in 30 days, six fixes and two unreachable! arms in product code. Its typed ContainerExecError (Launch/Refusal/Failure, refusal never borrowing an exit code) is the part worth keeping as the shared error.

Shutdown authority from current labels plus a full runtime ID, refusing pgid<=1, re-checking the container ID after a failed stop so a replacement container can never receive the old group's signal, and using a shell-portable group stop.
Reads named mounts from the final immutable Compose closure before creating host directories, so an isolated mount point is never invented. Narrow and single-purpose.

The typed decoder for Compose ps, inspect and stats: ContainerStatus, ContainerLifecycle and ContainerHealth are decided once from the runtime's own fields, with a serde shape for inspect. 17 tests at mean 8.2 cover the status table. Its health vocabulary is then re-decoded by health.rs and readiness.rs, which is those modules' finding.

A model doc: a runtime is skipped only when it is proven unable to own running containers, participation is resolved from every Docker endpoint it could be using, and detection never launches a runtime. Unknown keeps inventory authoritative rather than dropping it.

The single process-spawning owner with typed timeout handling and a test clock. But the one job has fourteen entry points - run_command_capture{,_allow_failure,_os,_os_with_env,_os_with_env_until,_with_timeout,_with_timeout_and_env,_with_absolute_deadline,_allow_failure_with_deadline,_allow_failure_with_absolute_deadline}, run_detached_{with_env,streaming_with_env,with_env_until}, run_private_detached - so callers choose a spelling rather than pass a mode. Proof is 24 tests at mean 6.4 with process-fixture oracles.

Bounded VM-side probe with four distinct verdicts, and Unknown never blocks bring-up or counts as healthy. The probe classifies its own token text rather than an exit code, which is a deliberate transport choice (string-matching a fixed probe script).

Per-check probing and the readiness wait budget are proportionate, and HealthWaitError separates NotReady from a definite StatusMismatch so a budget is not blamed for a wrong answer. But the healthy/unhealthy/starting vocabulary is decoded here, again in exec/parse.rs:98-100 (compose status) and again in health/readiness.rs HealthState::parse, so the same fact has three decoders.

Readiness diagnostics are strong: typed ServiceHealth, shared-failure signature and a next action. Ownership and decoding are not: it parses health status strings independently of exec/parse.rs and health.rs, and its inspect-JSON health parse sits beside the compose-ps parse in parse.rs.

Small typed observation: parses two real host load formats, refuses implausible measurements, and treats saturation as evidence about the host rather than the service. Tests cover both formats, the saturation rule and the refusal.

Crate-root facade: re-exports, effigy_home, user-global preference readers, driver labels and the typed catalog network contract. The user-global readers have no direct test and are only exercised indirectly through backend selection, so proof is weak rather than absent.

BackendId, registry, request/report types and the ContainerBackend trait are the right single vocabulary, but ContainerBackendDetection::from_env_and_path decides the backend from the environment as well as backend.rs's exact_backend, so the crate has two detection owners. ContainerManagerError carries only two variants while most failures are strings elsewhere, and the backend trait has one implementor.

Mount-string resolution is one owner with typed interpolation errors, but it re-parses the mount grammar that also appears as parse_mount_parts in policy/inline_workspace.rs:191, workspace/compose_rewrite.rs:670, workspace/ownership.rs:322 and container_runtime_prep/mod.rs:1932, and looks_like_bind_mount_source exists twice. Proof is three table tests (mean 7.0).
Typed cache list/prune request with side-effect class and confirmation. Small and single-purpose; its policy is proven through ops/mod.rs tests.
Typed data operations; import/pull/seed require confirmation while export and dump do not, matching which direction writes host versus runtime state.
Typed captured/shell exec request; side-effect class and no-confirmation policy are stated once.
Typed up/down/reset; wipe-data is Distinguished from recreate by its side-effect class and only wipe-data demands confirmation.

Typed operation plan: one side-effect class per operation family and a confirmation policy derived from it, so callers decide on a type instead of a command name. The per-family files own their own mapping.
Typed read operations, always ReadsRuntime and never confirmed.
The side-effect and confirmation vocabulary with a documented rule that only bring-up consumes declared container secrets.
Typed volume list/prune. Prune always confirms because the operation has no assume_yes flag; that asymmetry with cache prune is a surface question, not a failure.

A bounded one-release translation of retired compose_file environments into catalog fragments, with each fragment carrying the services it translates and any key a fragment cannot express refused rather than approximated. Migrate writes exactly these fragments, so before/after render is identical.

Pure planning for data_from volume sharing: typed VolumeDataHandover, only services declared identically in both environments are borrowed, and the ensure commands are returned for the runner rather than executed here. Four tests at mean 6.5, the weakest proof in the policy layer.

Scoped alias resolution for Effigy-owned host execution: the canonical declared alias is resolved to this checkout's own backing service before the child starts, with declared and scoped names as typed values rather than string rewriting at the call site.

Environment references are validated at policy load with the offending key and the valid names, and resolved later from typed facts (endpoint, origin, apex, https port); an unknown reference is a load failure, not an empty value. Six tests at mean 6.3, several of them fixture-level.

Owns the effective host map and scope rewriting; scope kind, route kind, cookie domain and relying party are typed, and the apex rewrite keeps every route under one scoped name. Three builder entry points (build_host_map, build_host_map_including_listeners, add_managed_listener_routes) for one mapping job; fold the listener variant into the builder.

Loads the inline-workspace container policy and resolves exec working directories; it re-parses mount strings with its own parse_mount_parts:191 instead of mount_spec.rs, which is the duplication noted there. No direct tests.

The policy loader, with typed CreationPolicyStage descriptions so progress is named in order. It has accumulated entry-point variants for the same load: load_container_policy, _with_workspace, _for_creation, _for_creation_observed, _for_qualification_inputs, prepare_container_policy, plus exec target and working-dir loaders; 1,034 lines and 42 commits in 30 days. Collapse observed/qualification into a mode parameter.
Namespace file only; it names the policy modules and holds no logic.

The effective policy's typed vocabulary: attach/compose-source enums, host process and listener types, route and data peer types, shared bindings, and a ContainerPolicyError that separates manifest, catalog, invocation and read failures with the failing path.

Prepare-only bind-source creation with the rule stated in the module doc: Effigy creates only the media and Composer-cache directories it owns, and a replaced symlink is re-refused rather than written through. Both properties are tested.

Pinned host-port decoding with the OS-assigned form explicitly pinning nothing, and a conflict check that names the holder while treating this project's own published port as no conflict. Four focused behaviour tests.
Project-name derivation, scoping and the uniqueness validation that refuses two environments resolving to one Compose project. Typed helpers; three direct tests at mean 7.0.

The render closure and its publication boundary: 'host rendering is an in-memory file closure, only Prepare publishes it', with typed Rendered (closure, path, shared renders) and a Named/Inline request enum that keeps the two workspace forms distinct.

A documented nerdctl limitation turned into one rewriting rule: exec-form health checks become shell form with each argument quoted for /bin/sh, while Docker keeps the exec form. Two functions, both tested.
Owns state home, object directory, prepare/publish/reset/verify and recorded-backend reads for the render closure, keeping publication in one place. Churn is 14 commits but the surface is coherent.

Compose interpolation for the VM backend with genuinely careful custody: a fresh random name not derived from contents, O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, mode 0600 inside a verified 0700 directory, and typed InterpolationLocation/Descriptors. It also builds compose invocation args, which compose.rs and colima.rs do too, so the argv owner is not single.

A documented workaround (effigy#383/#371) that keeps the restart policy out of the rendered file and applies it after start, so a re-up does not recreate a service; typed RestartPolicyStage names each step. The patch layer is justified by the bug it prevents, though apply_after_start{,_observed,_shared_observed} is a third variant family.

Declaration validation and the rendered-runtime validation pass, with 236 string literals of specific, actionable refusals naming paths and keys. Six direct tests at mean 8.3 plus the policy test suite.
Seven-line re-export shim over generated_compose; it adds a name, not a mechanism. Consolidate into policy_support/generated_compose.rs and export from there.

Generates the whole runtime Compose document: scope labels, volume borrow, port/media/host-mount/workspace-source policies, shared-service bindings and hashing, in 2,139 lines with 54 commits in 30 days and seven fix commits. Workspace-source shaping is also done in render/vm.rs, workspace.rs and artifact_source.rs, so the source binding has several owners. Generation should be split from the per-policy appliers.

Single owner of container report shaping with 33 builders; nothing else builds these payloads. Shape repetition is high: cache list/global and volume list/prune builders are near-identical (821/906/1030, 1161/1242) and the module works from ad-hoc Option/string fields rather than the typed operation results. Simplify by sharing the list/prune shaping and annotating the human string from the typed entry.

Materializes the runtime DNS override for gateway routes and resolves the runtime gateway address, with an observed (deadline-bounded) variant and a typed route set. 16 commits in 30 days but a single mechanism.
Three-line namespace for dns/retire/scope; no logic.

Typed retirement outcome: removed, kept with a reason, and failed with the runtime's own error, so 'ok' is exactly 'nothing failed' and remaining() lists what is still there. Persistence is a label fact (persist=true) rather than a name guess.
The scope label vocabulary (checkout, scope, managed, project) in one small module so generated Compose and retirement agree on label names. No direct tests.

Attached-session planning and command rendering, but the managed shell/exec command strings it builds are also built in container_command/support.rs and exec_command/surface.rs:1585-format_args territory, so host-invocation rewriting has more than one owner. The mode and plan types themselves are typed.

Workspace resolution, ownership targets, extra-mount decisions and guest isolation in 1,409 lines. The mount grammar is re-parsed here (path_is_within:394) as in policy/validation.rs:680, and the workspace-source binding is also shaped in generated_compose.rs, render/vm.rs and artifact_source.rs. The decision types are typed and tested.

Rewrites workspace mounts and service environment into a direct Compose document. But it re-implements the mount grammar (parse_mount_parts:670, looks_like_bind_mount_source:706) that mount_spec.rs and ownership.rs also own, path mapping (map_compose_paths:760, normalize_runtime_rewrite_paths:721) that workspace.rs also does, and workspace-source rewriting that generated_compose.rs and render/vm.rs also do. 908 product lines with three fixes.

Typed builders for each host integration mount (git config, ssh config/known_hosts/agent/dir, mkcert CA, composer home and cache) plus the workspace runtime environment, with test-only host overrides behind explicit guards. Homogeneous and single-purpose.

Builds adopted system-isolation mounts and refuses empty, absolute or escaping relative paths with the manifest path in the message. The volume name is derived from std DefaultHasher (efi-iso-{:016x}), whose output is unspecified across Rust releases, so a toolchain change can silently rename a persistent volume and orphan data. Use a specified digest.

User-global library mounts under a stable /workspace-libraries root. A missing host path is skipped silently by design (a developer's config may name a machine-specific path) while a basename collision is a hard error; the silent skip is a deliberate, documented fail-open with no diagnostic sink, so it is honest but loses the fact. One uncited test path covers it.

Owns the workspace ownership plan and repair authority, typed by mount kind (owned disposable, rust cache, repaired). It also owns a second copy of the mount grammar (parse_mount_parts:322, looks_like_bind_mount_source:340) shared with compose_rewrite.rs and mount_spec.rs.

An opt-in bounded exec surface: one absolute deadline, independent stdout/stderr budgets enforced while reading, and validation before any effect - all good. But it is a second implementation of the container shell command path beside lifecycle::run_container_shell, which the doc itself names as the unbounded sibling; the bounded form should be the one path with a mode, not a parallel runner.
The same four-arm list/prune wrapper as volume.rs, with its own copies of the --repo refusal and confirmation. Consolidate with volume.rs: one guard, one confirmation, two thin operation bindings.
Closeout for a failed or interrupted up: reset-wipe confirmation, cleanup of a partial bring-up, and the interrupted-up closeout text that says what was left running. Six tests at mean 7.2.

Attribution comes from the creation owner's journal under one absolute deadline, never from inventory or labels; a stalled read resolves to TimedOut and cannot attribute anything. Small and directly tested.

Data commands (pull-production, seed, dump, import, export) with confirmation gating on the destructive ones and a shared-service path. 780 product lines with no module doc; proof is 18 tests at mean 6.7, several of them fixture-level.
The data hook execution surface kept separate from the data command; no direct test of its own.
Prompt rendering for destructive data actions, kept apart from execution; no direct test of its own, exercised through data command tests.

Excellent private credential transport: create_new 0600 inside a verified 0700 directory, O_NOFOLLOW, no rewrite, partial write removed, bootstrap refuses rather than running without the credential, and the password never enters argv. It duplicates shared_credentials.rs almost verbatim (valid_env_name:129, private_credential_root:140, ensure_private_directory:151) - one private credential-file owner, two callers.

Route registration for a container environment with typed RegisteredGatewayRoute and LiveListenerConflict, declared-route preflight that refuses another environment's live claim, and gateway-service readiness detail that names the exited service. 1,419 lines, 41 commits in 30 days and five fixes; entry points multiply (ensure_gateway_running_for_container{,_with}, register_..._for_verified_container{,_observed}, wait_for_gateway_service_ports_ready{,_with,_observed}).

Whole-environment handover: preflight everything that can refuse, stop only same-checkout conflicts with ordinary down semantics, then start the requested environment, and record the handover so the stopped environment's up restarts it. 39 commits and four fixes in 30 days is the cost of that ordering.
Command wrapper that builds the scoped host map (including managed listeners) and labels the checkout's real scope kind so an ephemeral clone is not reported as a linked worktree. No direct test.

Up, down, status, stats, logs and shell in one file: 4,120 lines, 143 commits in the last 30 days and 150 in 90, eight fix commits, with run_container_up alone running from 150 to 1332 and carrying its own Step machine and two unreachable! arms. Each subcommand is its own mechanism with its own failure handling, so a 4k-line file with that churn is where regression risk concentrates. 34 tests at mean 7.0.
Small liveness probe with two tests at 9.

Refuses a foreign fragment before writing, stages and renames each file, restores the manifest and removes written directories on any failure, and re-renders to prove the render is unchanged. Covered by container_migrate_tests.

The `effigy container` dispatcher: parses into typed subcommand structs and renders one report envelope. 629 lines and 37 commits in 30 days, and the 'does not accept --repo' refusal is written five times here and in cache.rs, volume.rs, lifecycle.rs and profile.rs instead of one shared guard. One unreachable! encodes a parser invariant.

The one composition of load + declaration validation + rendered-runtime validation that the container command, workspace command and doctor share, so all three refuse the same policy the same way. No direct test of its own.

The profile command surface (list/create/start/stop/recover) over machine-level Colima profiles. Profile inventory and lifecycle are also owned by colima.rs and exec/colima_runtime.rs, and list_colima_profiles is defined in both this file (759) and colima_runtime.rs (1034). One unreachable! encodes a parser invariant; 16 tests at mean 7.0.

The readiness wait with evidence (820 product lines): a typed ReadinessEnd/ReadinessReport, each service named while waiting, a stack whose unready services share one failure diagnosed instead of waited out, and one absolute observation deadline. 28 commits but one coherent job.
Thin `container render` command: prints the published closure, shared renders and catalog sources, JSON or text, and never publishes. No direct test; exercised through CLI output tests.

The one producer of ReservedGuestInput: every field has an owner and an observation, planning and observation are split at the gated apply, and both halves share one absolute publication deadline so a delay cannot extend a probe. It never applies Compose or switches a selector. 47 tests.
Applies the restart policy after up and reports the typed stage; two focused tests.

Label-based retirement: typed Inventory/Owned/Group, ownership from the runtime's own labels, a report that separates removed, kept and failed, gateway release by checkout path, and unlabelled resources kept rather than swept. 13 tests at mean 8.2.
Retires stacks whose checkout is gone, with a typed PathState: a relative or unnormalised label is Unknown and reported, never guessed as dead. Two focused tests.
The repo-scope resolution used by every container command, with a typed ContainerRepoScope so a manifest-less invocation is a distinct case rather than a string error. Four tests at mean 6.2.

Resolves and materializes the container secret runtime (required-secret refusal, resolution, private key mode 0600), with three fix commits behind it. Its 11 tests average 6.5, which is the weakest proof in this file group.

The same private credential-file mechanism as data_credentials.rs (copied valid_env_name, private_credential_root, ensure_private_directory) for shared data targets, with its own 0600/0700 create_new/remove discipline. Consolidate into one credential-file module; only the transport (host env vs colima ssh) differs. Two tests.

Shared-service data operations: production pull, seed and hooks with confirmation, delegating credential transport to shared_credentials.rs. 372 product lines are proportionate; 21 tests at mean 6.5 leave much of the shared-service path exercised only through fixtures.

Resolves a container shell session and the workspace effigy refresh, with bounded twins (resolve_container_shell_session_bounded, maybe_refresh_workspace_effigy_for_shell_bounded) beside the unbounded functions, so each rule exists in two spellings. Eight tests at mean 7.2.
Runner-side live-step helper: names the restart-policy stage actually in flight so a stalled read is named instead of claiming an update was sent, re-exporting the shared ComposeSteps/TimedStep.

The runner's grab-bag: readiness wait, exec-error classification, pinned-port availability, host-alias installation, volume removal and nine annotate_* functions that push presentation onto reports. 1,591 product lines and 72 commits in 30 days with three fixes. The annotate_* family belongs with report shaping (containers/src/report.rs) and the runtime capture helpers with exec; 42 tests at mean 6.7.

A fail-closed interface scaffold with no production caller: prepare_workspace_quiet, prepare_supervisor_quiet, negotiate_private_bound and run_compose_discard unconditionally return Unavailable, and the custody types are documented placeholders ('no constructor is exposed'). git grep finds the identifiers only in this file and its own test module, so the refusal behaviour is proven by nothing but itself. Its public path and any docs naming it must be retired with it.

A four-arm subcommand wrapper whose two global arms repeat the same --repo refusal text and the same confirmation call shape as cache.rs. Consolidate the global/--repo guard and confirmation into one helper shared with cache.rs and mod.rs.

Execution-only recovery for the private Linux builder: a retained builder keeps its admission, every build targets a freshly verified immutable ID, only verified artifact bytes reach the caller, and the /workspace source bind is read-only. 31 commits and five fixes in 30 days is the cost of that custody.

Stages the builder's exact source closure from git ls-files into the checkout's child of the profile mount, with explicit exclusion rules and refusals for symlinks or missing tracked files. It is a third owner of staged-source placement beside artifact_source.rs (which owns StagePlan ownership proof) and export/compilation state; the two should be one staging owner. Two tests.

A well-specified integration contract: fixed step order, attempt recorded before the effect, deadline checked between adapter calls, and unwind that reports unsettled steps instead of claiming success. But from_attempted() returns Result<_, &'static str> and still calls unwrap() on STEPS.iter().position(), so a malformed journal panics where the function's own signature promises a refusal.

The gateway readiness stage for a task's container runtime, with every side effect injected so the stage can be proven; it skips only when the policy declares no gateway surface. No direct test of its own, exercised through the mod tests.

The task-runtime preparation orchestrator, and the only large module in the domain with no module doc at all. 1,941 lines and 67 commits in 30 days with five fixes, holding the activation plan/report, Cargo-input refresh, live checkout mount verification, image platform parsing, frozen compose config hashing and host bind directory creation. 39 tests at mean 7.2 do not make that pile one responsibility.

Preparation stages: mount sources, the one compose up, exec readiness and alias reconciliation, each with injected effects. reconcile_runtime_aliases_stage_using is a pure pass-through that only calls its closure (74-80), so the stage adds an indirection with no behaviour. Remove it.
Two tiny typed stages: is the primary service running, and bring the stack up only when it was not. No direct test, exercised through the mod tests.

Two real validation stages (policy, backend) with typed errors. The dispatcher's match has a `_ => Ok(())` arm, so any stage added to RuntimeActivationStage validates nothing and reports success; enumerate the stages or refuse the unknown one.

A rigorous bounded capture with its contract written down: budgets enforced while reading, one absolute deadline spanning spawn/drain/reap, concurrent drains, and only the process group Effigy created is signalled. It is a second bounded-capture implementation beside container_command/bounded_exec.rs (same deadline + budget + owned-group mechanism for the shell path), so the crate has two owners for one contract. 13 tests at mean 6.7.

The deadline fixture seam: a thread-local reading that only test builds set, so a bounded proof freezes the clock, runs the real spawn/drain/terminate and then expires deterministically, while the production cfg compiles to Instant::now(). The seam is explicitly scoped to the proving thread.

The exec router: typed ExecArgs, surface activation, and two named strategy predicates (does the strategy require a workspace effigy install, does a routed task exec) so the decision is a boolean fact rather than duplicated in callers. 25 commits in 30 days and one `_with` injection variant.

Resolves the exec surface (default, named, running named), builds the alias table and the raw exec argv into typed options, and maps the host cwd. No direct tests; exercised through the exec command tests.

The exec transport: routed task exec args, credential bootstrap, owned compose exec plans, verified native invocation, compose-exec argv parsing and capability detection, in 1,472 product lines with no module doc. Process spawning is exec/process.rs's job and bounded capture is bounded.rs's, so this file is a third spawn path; its own format_args is a copy of exec/process.rs:987. 17 tests at mean 6.9.
The Colima side of exec transport in its own module beside the host side, which is the right split; seven tests at mean 7.7 cover the SSH/nerdctl transport.

The one place lanes A/B/C meet: placement detection, client capability, guest auth, the pinned channel, dispatch and rendering, with typed ChannelError/ChannelOutcome/GuestPlacement and an explicit rule that a host refusal is final with no guest fallback. The doc states what it does not own. 2,076 product lines and 43 commits in 30 days, with a 500-line WorkspaceClient impl; 97 tests. Rated as the module-group root although the brief's `workspace_client/**` glob does not literally match the file.

Supervisor-local activation with a written boundary: only command intent crosses the process boundary, never a seal, reservation, handle or deadline. Staged-object observation with the key property written down: the running executable's SHA-256 is read once before any observation and every reply names it, so a replaced object cannot report evidence for the object it replaced. Reads no credential and sends no channel frame.

The Level 1 non-interactive forwarding seam under Tom's 2026-11-01 ruling: no PTY, stdin at EOF, one authenticated connection held from admission to the exact run's terminal outcome, typed InteractiveRequest refusals and a retained-position stream read.

The owner of the session's serving custody: binds the handoff, refuses Unpublished/WrongSession/KeyReleased/Unswitched states, classifies recovery and keeps serving until the session settles. The refusals are the contract written as types.

The workspace terminal owner and retained-stream adapter: every input validated against the live attachment, bounded pending input, and one absolute retained-coordinate system with no second replay store.

Workspace permission preparation with typed targets, mode and plan, and an in-file MemoryAccessBackend double so the decision path is proven without touching a real filesystem. Only three commits in 30 days; heavy test coverage (50 tests).
